title: Advertising Time
subtitle: Feeling empty inside? Dine on the latest ads.

items.text: Advertising Time
The Headonion Show

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Later, your faithful journalist discovered the final diary entry of the leader of Fingers's gang, the Cheshire Cats, penned on his deathbed.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: In this heart-wrenching journal, we found these words.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: The Last Confessions of a Gang Boss

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: I know my body's failing me, breath by breath. As the cough gets worse, I take stock of my life.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: I came from the Diego family. The first fifty years, I fought just to stay alive. Here, I've found work that lets me live.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: On the streets, people fear me. They show me the respect I deserve. That's the kind of prestige I've earned.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: But when night falls and everything goes silent, I lie awake, feeling empty inside. The life I've lived makes it hard to love anyone, yet it's something I crave.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: Money gives you what you need to stay alive, but love—love gives you what you need to live.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: MacGuffin the Knife is the only thing in my life I've ever truly loved.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: I tell everyone I meet there's enough Rheingold in his belly to buy all of New York.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: But, it's not true, not really. I'm the only one who truly understands how this mutt's worth more than any Rheingold.

items.speaker: Gang Boss
items.text: I've taken many lives, but never has a single drop of that blood touched his fluffy coat.
Black Iron Forest

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: So ...
A sudden hush, an awkward group of people, two dogs, and a corpse yet to be dealt with.
AJ gestures politely to Mercuria.

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: He's saying his farewells, you strange little lady.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof! Woof, woof, woof?

items.speaker: "Doggie"
items.text: The puppy seeks clarification.

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: Yep. Turns out the mutt didn't have anything in him at all.
Panzo sounds exhausted, as though he has just faced the darkest night of his life.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: What's next for you? Will you keep up your crime spree? Are there plans to hit any more gas stations?

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: Don't know. I'm ... tired.

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: Goddamn it! Don't you get it yet?

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: There's no Rheingold, no MacGuffin the Knife. It's just a mutt!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof—woof, woof.

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: Screw this! I'm taking a break—a real one. You know, I've always wanted to leave this place behind.

items.speaker: Panzo
items.text: I'm heading to the shore, find a place where I can see the waves, enjoy some good food ...
Mercuria and Pickles watch as they sign and whine as they walk off, still silently dreaming with one another as they squeeze back into their rundown car.
The door shuts with a solid "thud."
Still under Mercuria and Pickles' gaze, they drive off into the distance.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Whuh-woof—?

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: So, what's the plan now? What do we do with this dog?

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof?

items.speaker: "Doggie"
items.text: The puppy is concerned.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Oh, Pickles, you know I'm not talking about you. I'm talking about the other one.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: MacGuffin the Knife.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Maybe we ought to start with a new name? What do you think?
Mercuria takes out the picture of MacGuffin the Knife, and sets it ablaze with her lighter.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Whuh-woof, woof ... woof, woof, woof, hrm?
The photo of MacGuffin the Knife burns away, its ash floating into the air before landing on Fingers's pale, lifeless face.
Promenade

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Just imagine—if Fingers hadn't gone after MacGuffin the Knife, he might still be with us.
By the shore, at sunset. Pickles licks the ice cream in Mercuria's hand.
The gentle breeze lifts Mercuria's hair, while the journalist's intermittent analysis comes in via the communicator.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: This thing, which he thought would open the doors to a new world, instead set him on the path to his own ruin.
Half-melted ice cream drips onto the ground, each drop like a thought tapping out a rhythm.
The Chihuahua pokes its head out from Mercuria's arms.
She rises to her feet.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Let's go.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Hrm? Woof, woof, woof, woof?

items.speaker: "Doggie"
items.text: The puppy is concerned.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Oh, you mean this pup here?

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof ... woof, woof, whuh-woof.

items.speaker: "Doggie"
items.text: The puppy has a proposal.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: You mean a shelter, right?
Mercuria sets the Chihuahua aside.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof ...?

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: The shelter. I remember that place.
She blinks her eyes.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: A bed soaked in the scent of mushrooms, morning dew dripping from dried leaves.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Clothes hung out to dry in the yard are only remembered once the rain starts. And so, we wore the rain.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Good times, friends arrive and leave, one by one. Like notes in a melody.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Summer comes, the fans break, everyone cries.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Winter, the bugs breed, and everyone waits for what is to come.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: All of this—just a mere touch of this—is enough to captivate.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: But I had to leave.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: In the new world, there is always something waiting. Hunger, poverty, misery, strife, nights blend into days, danger, everywhere. They lie in wait, and we must face them.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: A dog, a joke, or a few specks of dust shining in the sunlight—each is vital.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Don't be afraid.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: He will live. He has a potent, healthy energy within, pushing him to grow and survive.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: He will find a place to belong, one much better than we could ever give him.
The dog takes a moment to think, then nods his head.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Grrr ...

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: So, you lived in a shelter before?
A journalist always cuts to the heart of the matter.
But Mercuria offers no reply.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Okay. Just a thought, we might be able to borrow an infrared positioning device with extended range from the suitcase. If you're worried, then we'll always be able to locate him.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: We can check in on him, and make sure he's safe wherever he goes in this big bad world.
At that moment, the Chihuahua twitches its little nose, pokes its head out, and its earring sparkles brightly in the sunlight.
Its sharp eyes catch a glimpse of red in the distance. It is a red balloon.
With a swift push of its front paws, the Chihuahua jumps from the stool.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Hey!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof!

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: What happened? What's going on?
The Chihuahua's quick, nimble steps propel it forward at speed, as it disappears into the crowd.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof!

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: It ran off.
Mercuria and Pickles watch in disbelief as the Chihuahua sprints off.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Looks like all our worries were for nothing.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: He's off chasing his own "MacGuffin."
The red balloon drifts under the blue sky, and the world remains unchanged.
Pickles steals a quiet look at Mercuria.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof, woof ... woof, woof, woof.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: ... Grrr ... Grrr, grrr.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof, woof. Woof, woof.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Well then, let's extend our thanks to Pickles for his insightful account. And with that, our in-depth investigation draws to a close. If any viewers have further contributions to offer, you can reach out to your humble journalist ONiON backstage.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: By the way, if there are any canine communication experts among our viewers, feel free to contact me urgently. We're hiring paid dog-speak translators.

items.speaker: Advertisement I
items.text: Lucky Mangoes ripen under special exclusively patented lighting, and when they arrive at your local Lucky Supermarket, you'll find yourself in a realm of happiness.

items.speaker: Advertisement II
items.text: Still fretting over hair loss? Stressing over sagging skin? With SuperStar Energy, you're just one sip away from a new you, and two sips from looking ten years younger! Now available for just $6.99! That's right, take home a super healthy can of liquid energy for only $6.99 today!

items.speaker: Advertisement III
items.text: Welcome to a new era of credit! No co-signers or credit checks. Buy anything without worrying about your bank balance! True happiness has finally arrived, and you don't need to pay a dime for it!
Police Office
The TV shuts off with a loud "click." A towering figure in a police uniform blocks the screen.

items.speaker: Officer
items.text: Stop watching that crap, and listen up.

items.speaker: Officer
items.text: There's been an update in the Black Iron Forest shooting case. We've just received an anonymous tip pointing to the identities of the perps.

items.speaker: Officer
items.text: The victim was a former member of the Cheshire Cats, known within the gang as "Fingers."

items.speaker: Officer
items.text: The suspects are believed to be two retired contract killers, and gang violence may be a factor in the motive.

items.speaker: Officer
items.text: Alright, get to work, people.
WANTED
Wanted: Panzo and AJ.
Lobby, Suitcase

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Well, who's this now?
Unable to sleep, the night-blind bounty hunter stumbles into someone in the dark.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: Oh, I'm making a call.
Mercuria lowers the phone receiver, the air around her filled with the scent of herbal incense.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Oh, Miss Mercuria. I didn't expect to find you 'round here so late.
Mercuria spins around, grabs a glass of water from the table, and offers it to Argus.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: This should offer your eye some relief.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: How did you know?
She doesn't answer, instead heading to the center of the common room and placing a circle of lit candles there.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: This trip ...

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Huh?
Smoke rises, the pendulum sways, and the ceremony is about to begin.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I see energy slipping into death, but I cannot intervene.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: However, by placing candles on his body, I can help him tap into energy from another plane.

items.speaker: Mercuria
items.text: I hope he remains untouched by the chaotic spirits of that world.
Mercuria softly says the last of her words, then begins to dance. As she does, a quiet tenderness and sadness flow from her movements, barely perceptible to most.

items.speaker: Subtitles
items.text: This show is inspired by actual events. To protect the privacy of the individuals involved, their real names have been changed.

items.speaker: Subtitles
items.text: All other content has not been altered.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: In response to the overwhelming complaints alleging the content of this special to be illogical, irrational, or just plain false, let me take this moment to restate the end credits message.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Whether this program is rooted in real events is yet to be determined, its authenticity is left to the interpretation of the audience. More importantly, this program does not claim to hold the final truth concerning all related incidents.

items.speaker: Advertisement I
items.text: Organic fruit, health and quality guaranteed—is there really anything more important in life?
